summary: The change adds a build-folder slot that is enforced in code. Only one job at a time can hold a build folder. It is a one-entry SlotQueue under <state>/build-folder/, used through BuildFolder and take_build_folder in disk.rs. dispatch in run/mod.rs takes it after planning and before the baseline checks, and a resumed job takes it before its checks. When the guard is dropped it removes the job's target/ and the holder file, and only then frees the slot. At dispatch, dispatch_disk_gate no longer holds a job when the shortfall is explained by the named holder's measured folder; every other low-disk case still holds. The wait is left out of wall_time_execution through RunClock. max_concurrency stays 2 on line 205 (the base already read 2). CHANGELOG, a new appended D188 and a new section 11 in agent-and-build-slots.md record the design and its alternatives. I ran the 12 build_folder tests, the live-config test, the backtest and the changed lifecycle test; all pass. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test checks pass. They show both jobs inside planning together, the second producer starting only after the first job's folder is gone, a peak of 1 holder measured on disk, and no hold for a waiting job while simulated free space is below the gate. A job short of disk for its own reasons is still held. The folder is freed after landed, rejected, no-change, held and killed jobs. The remaining issues are minor: three changed files are outside the deliverables list, and the criterion-1 test calls go twice on threads rather than running the drain.
